title: POC weekly — model roadmapping & version escrow sync
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on finalizing model selection matrix, introducing the idea of a version 'escrow' for emergency rollbacks, and scheduling a staged latency + quality benchmark. Discussed SOC2/KMS questions and agreed next steps for manifest and staging tests.
topics: Model selection tradeoffs (latency v cost v quality)
Security/compliance: KMS, audit logs, SOC2 evidence
Staging echo tests and latency bench schedule
next_steps: Redwood to send draft pinned-manifest + version escrow proposal (Lena) by 2027-11-05
Customer to run two staging echo tests with shadow traffic and share seq-level failures (Marcus) by 2027-11-09
Redwood to schedule 2-hour latency/throughput bench on dedicated instance and invite Priya (Jonah) week of 2027-11-15
Share SOC2 attestation and encryption/KMS docs (Lena) by 2027-11-04
action_items: Lena Park — Draft pinned-manifest + rollback playbook — due 2027-11-05
Jonah Kim — Prepare latency bench checklist & infra runbook — due 2027-11-13
Marcus Shaw — Run shadow/staging echo tests and capture KV cache profiles — due 2027-11-09
Priya Desai — Provide 3 representative prompt sets and quality thresholds — due 2027-11-06
transcript:
[00:00] Lena: Alright everyone, thanks for joining. This is Lena from Redwood, AE, and Jonah is with me on the call for the deep bench. Uh, we want to go over model selection matrix and a, a small proposal we re calling a version escrow for emergency rollback.
[00:18] Priya: Hi, thanks. Priya here. Sorry for the late join, had a standup overrun. We have Marcus and Linda on.
[00:26] Marcus: Hey hi this is Marcus, Platform. Good to see you.
[00:29] Linda: Linda, CTO, quick hello.
[00:31] Jonah: Quick agenda — results from last week's staging run, pick model candidates to pin, discuss the escrow/manifest approach, map fallback routes, and schedule a latency bench.
[00:42] Priya: Sounds good. Last week we ran three models from Redwood's catalog: rdx-3b-q, rdx-7b, and a client-side tuned 7b-8k. Results were noisy but overall the 7b gave best F1 on our extraction tests. Latency on 7b was 190ms median, 350 p95 in our Puerto region.
[01:05] Jonah: Okay, and the 3b quantized run — was that using continuous batching or single-shot?
[01:09] Priya: Single-shot, we didn't enable batching for that run. We can re-run later with batching to see CP consumption.
[01:15] Lena: Quick clarifying Q — when you say p95 350, is that with KV cache warm or cold?
[01:20] Marcus: Cold. Cache warmed the p95 drops to about 210ms. Also we noticed a couple of tokenization mismatches on the extraction set, probably prom— prompt normalization stuff.
[01:29] Jonah: Good, that matters for pinning decisions. So preliminarily, it seems rdx-7b is the quality leader, rdx-3b-q is cost-efficient but needs batching and maybe a quantization profile tweak.
[01:42] Linda: Our risk tolerance is low for mis-extractions, so leaning to quality. But cost is non-trivial. If we pin 7b as primary, what's our escape hatch?
[01:51] Lena: Which is where the version escrow concept comes in — idea is we maintain an immutable pinned-manifest that lists primary+fallback variants, plus a small escrowed snapshot that Redwood can push into your private catalog under controlled conditions. It's like an emergency rollback artifact.
[02:08] Marcus: So escrow means you keep a copy of the model binary and the exact runtime config? How does that sit with our data residency and KMS policies?
[02:16] Jonah: Short answer: escrow manifest is metadata-first. For hosted pilots we store the manifest and references to model artifacts. For Private/Dedicated you'd get an export tarball with checksums, and keys are wrapped by your KMS. We discussed HSM/KMS in the security review — that flow remains consistent, we don't hold unencrypted keys.
[02:33] Priya: Okay that helps. Another operational Q — if we do an emergency cut to the fallback, do we want soft-fallback where we route a % of traffic or hard switch?
[02:42] Lena: We recommend canary + soft-fallback as first line: route 5-10% to fallback variant, compare essential metrics (latency, extraction accuracy), then escalate. The pinned manifest would include an auto-failover threshold and an operator contact list.
[02:55] Linda: And can the manifest specify model variants by behavior — e.g., embeddings v text-gen optimized? Because some of our flows use embeddings heavily.
[03:03] Jonah: Yes, the manifest supports per-route pinning. You can pin a different family for generating structured output vs embeddings. We also store quantization tier and allowed sequence lengths per variant.
[03:13] Marcus: We saw the KV cache helped a lot. When we route, do you preserve cache or is it lost on switch?
[03:19] Jonah: For soft-fallbacks, the runtime can attempt to warm the cache by shadowing requests to the fallback, so warm-up overlap is possible. For hard switch there is inevitable cold-start unless you pre-warm.
[03:30] Priya: On the quality side, we need a concrete rollback metric. If extraction F1 drops by >2 points over a 30-minute window, that's a trigger to initiate the canary.
[03:40] Lena: Good — we'll add that as a sample SLA metric on the draft manifest.
[03:45] Marcus: About security docs — Linda needs the SOC2 evidence and a breakdown of audit log retention.
[03:51] Lena: We'll attach the SOC2 report and a readme on audit log retention. For Private deployments logs can be forwarded to your SIEM and retention is on-prem configured.
[04:01] Linda: Also SSO and RBAC mapping — we need examples of role mappings for the operator flow.
[04:06] Lena: We'll include a sample SAML role map and recommended RBAC roles for canary operators.
[04:12] Priya: Can we see the actual manifest format? JSON or YAML?
[04:15] Jonah: Draft will be JSON for easy machine parsing, with fields: route, primary_model, fallback_models[], quant_profile, allowed_seq_len, failover_thresholds, rollforward_rules. We'll include a human-friendly doc too.
[04:28] Marcus: On the pinned-manifest: do you support multi-model hedging? Like split traffic across two models and pick majority answer?
[04:34] Jonah: Yes, you can configure hedging with voting or scorer-based arbitration. It's more expensive but useful for high-risk flows.
[04:42] Linda: Cost estimate? Hedging x2 obviously doubles token cost. We need a unit cost projection for a month of production traffic in our region.
[04:49] Lena: We'll provide a cost projection and sample runbook for hedging; we can also show a hybrid where embeddings are on a cheaper family and extraction on a quality family.
[04:59] Priya: Back to the catalog — we noticed some naming mismatches between Redwood catalog names and what we use internally. Can we get a concordance table?
[05:06] Lena: Yes, we'll include a concordance csv mapping Redwood identifiers to your internal labels.
[05:10] Marcus: Great. On staging tests — for next bench we want to include: warm+cold KV cache runs, 10k concurrent short requests, and 1k long seqs to simulate note generation.
[05:21] Jonah: Noted. We'll include sequence length distribution and tokenization diagnostics. Also will capture per-token latency breakdown.
[05:29] Priya: One thing we saw — a few transcripts had early truncation on longer seqs. Might be model token limit or runtime chunking.
[05:36] Jonah: Could be chunking heuristics or kernel memory. We'll instrument the chunk boundaries and provide a trace for each truncated request.
[05:44] Linda: For the escrow, who signs the manifest? We need tamper evidence.
[05:48] Lena: Manifest will be signed with Redwood's release key and also include a customer-side checksum step. For Private, we can support mutual signing with your key. That gives tamper-proof history.
[06:00] Marcus: Great. Can we talk briefly about rollback drills? We want to simulate an emergency rollback next month.
[06:06] Lena: Recommend a tabletop first, then a staged dry-run: day 1 run soft-fallback to 10%, day 2 escalate to 100% for 30 minutes then roll forward.
[06:15] Priya: We prefer to run during a low-traffic window. Marcus will propose dates.
[06:19] Marcus: I'll propose two windows next week.
[06:22] Jonah: On telemetry — what are the three must-have metrics for you during a canary?
[06:26] Priya: Latency p95, extraction F1, and error rate (5xx or model exceptions).
[06:31] Lena: Perfect, we'll bake those into the manifest as required observability.
[06:35] Linda: Any competitor concerns? We evaluated Anthropic's API but their latency in our region was higher; OpenAI's throughput was good but vendor lock-in is a worry. So the runway with Redwood's dedicated variant is attractive.
[06:48] Jonah: Noted. We'll include a small competitor appendix in the docs comparing throughput, latencies and escape clauses.
[06:56] Priya: Small nit — in the last bench, tokens-per-second metric looked wrong. It might be aggregation bug.
[07:01] Jonah: We'll recheck the aggregation logic and send corrected dashboards.
[07:05] Marcus: About the manifest again — can we include an automated rollback TTL so that if someone manually flips to fallback it's only for X hours unless explicitly extended?
[07:14] Lena: Yes — we can add rollback TTL and require a two-step confirmation for >TTL. That helps prevent accidental long-lived fallbacks.
[07:23] Priya: For the pinned versions, we want to lock minor versions but allow patch updates. Is that supported?
[07:28] Jonah: We support semver-style locks: you can pin by major.minor or exact commit. The escrow snapshot is the exact commit/quant profile.
[07:36] Linda: For auditability, include a changelog of who altered manifests and when.
[07:41] Lena: Audit logs are part of the operator trail; we will show example entries in the sample manifest.
[07:47] Marcus: Anything else on tech?
[07:49] Priya: I think we covered the big points. We need the pinned-manifest and also the SOC2 docs.
[07:55] Lena: Okay action recap — Lena sends draft manifest + security pack by Friday; Jonah schedules bench and runbook; Marcus runs staging shadow tests; Priya will provide prompts.
[08:06] Linda: Also, please include the manifest sample in both JSON and a human markdown explainer.
[08:11] Lena: Will do.
[08:13] Priya: One last question — can rollback be automatic on specific anomaly patterns or do you recommend manual?
[08:19] Jonah: We support automated rollback triggers but recommend manual with optional automation for well-tested thresholds. For pilot, start manual + alerting, then move to automated after drills.
[08:29] Marcus: Sounds good. I'll send windows for drills.
[08:33] Lena: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in the next couple of days with the artifacts.
[08:37] Linda: Thanks, bye.
[08:40] [meeting end — 54 minutes recorded total, includes pre/post buffer]
